apnews.com.notes: Cooperative newswire with a public corrections policy and named sourcing standards.

reuters.com.notes: International wire with a published Trust Principles document and a corrections process.

bbc.co.uk.notes: Public broadcaster with written editorial guidelines and an independent complaints process.

npr.org.notes: US public radio with editorial guidelines and corrections.

ft.com.notes: Specialist financial paper with a corrections column and named bylines.

cbc.ca.notes: Canadian public broadcaster with a journalistic standards guide.

dw.com.notes: German public international broadcaster with statutory editorial independence.

nytimes.com.notes: National paper with a public corrections page and standards editor.

theguardian.com.notes: Owned by the Scott Trust, with a readers' editor and open corrections.

washingtonpost.com.notes: National paper with published standards and a corrections process.

bloomberg.com.notes: Financial newswire with a public code of ethics.

france24.com.notes: France Médias Monde international broadcaster with a published charter.

dawn.com.notes: Pakistan's longest-running English paper, with named bylines and a corrections practice.

thehindu.com.notes: Indian national paper with a readers' editor.

thediplomat.com.notes: Specialist outlet focused on Asia-Pacific security and diplomacy.

politico.com.notes: Politics desk with named reporters and a corrections policy.

aljazeera.com.notes: International newsroom funded by Qatar. Ownership is public; treat state-aligned framing as a factor, not a reason to drop the source.

news.un.org.notes: Official United Nations outlet. Transparent about its institutional role; not an independent newsroom.

sky.com.notes: UK commercial broadcaster regulated by Ofcom. Faster headlines, more live-TV tone.

euronews.com.notes: Pan-European broadcaster with several shareholders and a shorter corrections trail than a newspaper.

africanews.com.notes: Pan-African broadcaster linked to Euronews. Useful regional coverage; thinner public standards page.

al-monitor.com.notes: Regional specialist. Useful on Middle East diplomacy; smaller corrections apparatus.

cnn.com.notes: Large international desk and a corrections page, with a history of sensational headlines.

newsapi.org.notes: Aggregator. Articles are scored against the outlet that published them, not against NewsAPI.

gnews.io.notes: Aggregator. Articles are scored against the outlet that published them.
